kartice.povzetek_sl: Background Bone cancer pain (BCP) is a debilitating complication of advanced cancer that substantially impairs physical function and emotional wellbeing. Current pharmacological treatments often provide incomplete analgesia and may be limited by adverse effects. Shikonin, a bioactive naphthoquinone derived from Lithospermum erythrorhizon, exhibits analgesic and anti inflammatory activities, but its effects and underlying mechanisms in BCP remain unclear. Bioluminescence imaging and hematoxylin eosin staining were used to characterize tumor development and bone pathology. kartice.povzetek_sl: Background Previous studies of drugs targeting mixed linage kinase type 3 (MLK3) and/or leucine rich repeat kinase type 2 (LRRK2) in sporadic Parkinsons disease (PD) have failed to meet clinical endpoints despite multiple lines of evidence implicating these kinases in pathogenesis. This has reduced enthusiasm for MLK3 and LRRK2 as druggable targets. Largely overlooked is the evidence that these targets remain valid but must be considered in combination to achieve a therapeutic outcome. This provides the rationale for this study. Methods We conducted a pilot study modeling early, pre-symptomatic PD with subsequent evaluation of therapeutic potential of a multi-kinase inhibitor (URMC-099) in alleviating disease pathology. Sprague Dawley rats received unilateral intranigral injections of low dose AAV-haSyn. After a two-week recovery period, all animals were administered either once-daily intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of URMC-099 or its vehicle control until their terminal endpoint. kartice.naslov: Proteome-wide discovery of novel diagnostic antigens for coccidioidomycosis
kartice.povzetek_sl: Coccidioidomycosis, commonly called Valley Fever (VF), caused by Coccidioides spp., is an understudied fungal disease that accounts for a substantial fraction of pneumonias in endemic areas. Diagnosis remains challenging because the mainstay of diagnosis is serology, and current assays have modest sensitivity in early infection. Discovery of new antigens could improve serologic detection early in disease. Here, we use PepSeq, a DNA-programmable serology platform, to represent the complete proteome of Coccidioides within a library of 244,000 DNA-barcoded peptides. By profiling antibody reactivity at the protein and epitope levels in VF patients, naturally infected pigtail macaques, and healthy controls, we identify numerous previously-unrecognized antigens and epitopes, including some shared between humans and macaque responses. When translated into a pooled peptide ELISA, we show that a subset of identified antigens can discriminate VF cases from controls in an independent cohort with high accuracy (AUC = 0.91). These findings establish high-dimensional peptide serology as a scalable approach for fungal antigen discovery and identify new targets for improved VF diagnosis.

kartice.povzetek_sl: Mesenchymal traits are associated with poor prognosis in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDA), but direct targeting of mesenchymal tumor cells remains a challenge. Metabolic profiling of tumor cells isolated from murine PDA and liver metastases (LM) revealed that LM rely more on the methionine cycle than does primary PDA. This metabolic shift was specifically associated with increased activation of the methionine cycle in mesenchymal tumor cells compared to differentiated tumor cells.
